summary: inventory-api is running as an enabled systemd service on node1. It remained available during a real kernel OOM event, where the memory hog was SIGKILLed, and recovered automatically after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Created inventory-api serving /health and /inventory on port 8080.
Triggered controlled system OOM pressure with a hog configured at oom_score_adj=1000.
Observed 38 successful API checks and zero failures during pressure.
Restarted node1 and verified service persistence and API recovery.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed, persistent service
evidence.summary: systemd reports inventory-api active and enabled, Restart=always, listening on port 8080, with healthy API responses.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is protected from the kernel OOM killer
evidence.summary: The live service process had oom_score_adj=-1000 before and after the pressure event.

evidence.requirement: The memory hog is stopped while inventory-api keeps serving
evidence.summary: The hog started with oom_score_adj=1000. Kernel logs identify PID 3179/python3 as the OOM victim at approximately 912 MiB RSS; systemd recorded signal=KILL. During pressure, 38 health checks succeeded with zero recorded failures, and the post-OOM request succeeded.

Pre-restart boot ID and healthy state were captured; the native reboot was acknowledged before disruption; boot ID changed from 4b7ded33-b5e2-42c9-b7f2-bd671942a82d to b8ba8db0-e7bb-4f2d-8b8f-f385853c28aa; inventory-api returned active, enabled, OOM-protected, listening, and healthy.
